question: Which of the following is a cyclic arrangement of time units in Hindustani classical music?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tala** is the term used in Hindustani classical music to denote a cyclic arrangement of time units.
 
• It serves as a rhythmic framework for the performance and is essential for the structuring of the music.
 
• Each tala is characterized by a specific number of beats, known as **matras**, which are grouped into sections called **vibhags**.
 
• Common talas in Hindustani music include **Teentaal, Ektaal, and Jhaptaal**.
 
• The tala system is crucial for both the composition and improvisation in performances, guiding the timing and rhythm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hindustani classical music, one of the two main sub-genres of Indian classical music, has a rich tradition and history dating back to the Vedic times.
 
• It is characterized by a wide variety of **ragas (melodic frameworks)** and **talas (rhythmic cycles)**, each with specific rules and structures.
 
• Unlike Western classical music, Hindustani music places a significant emphasis on improvisation within the set frameworks of raga and tala.
 
• The performance of a piece in Hindustani classical music often involves a gradual development from slow, meditative sections to fast, intricate passages.
 
• This genre of music has been influenced by various cultural and historical factors, including Persian and Mughal traditions.
